ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1 meter. It is tan or olive with two dark lateral stripes and a pale belly. Key features include a pointed snout, large eyes with round pupils, and a divided anal plate.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Psammophis schokari* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark longitudinal stripe running through the eye, bordered by thin, pale, cream-colored lines.
ai.habitat: *Psammophis schokari* inhabits arid, sandy deserts and semi-arid scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found in low-altitude, sparsely vegetated sandy plains.
ai.behavior: Forskål's Sand Snake is a highly active diurnal hunter that uses its exceptional speed and agility to pursue lizards across open, arid terrain.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Psammophis schokari* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–15 eggs. Breeding generally occurs during the warmer months, often peaking between spring and summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: Psammophis schokari occurs in the arid regions of northwestern India, primarily across Rajasthan and Gujarat, typically inhabiting sandy, low-elevation desert scrublands.
